result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.within_inter_cluster()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Score node pairs by the ratio of within- to inter-community common neighbors. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.within_inter_cluster()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Score node pairs by the ratio of within- to inter-community common neighbors. title: >- [Graph.within_inter_cluster()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Score node pairs by the ratio of within- to inter-community common neighbors. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Score node pairs by the ratio of within- to inter-community common neighbors. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L28768-L28829){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.within_inter_cluster( ebunch=None, delta=0.001, community="community", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Within-inter-cluster ratio](../assets/graphs/within-inter-cluster.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Four nodes in a square: A, B and D form community 0 (teal region) and C is community 1 (violet region). The candidate link A–D (dashed) has one common neighbor inside its community, B (accent), and one outside, C. The card divides 1 within by 1 inter plus delta 0.001, a score of 0.999." width="100%"} The within-inter-cluster score (Valverde-Rebaza and de Andrade Lopes, 2012) compares the common neighbors of two nodes that share their community with those that do not: `|within| / (|inter| + delta)`. Pairs in different communities score `0`. A high score means the pair's shared contacts sit inside their own community, a strong sign of a missing intra-community link. The graph is treated as undirected and simple. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ebunch]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[Union[int, str], Union[int, str]]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of `(u, v)` pairs to score. If `None` (default), every pair of non-adjacent nodes is scored. [delta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.001]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Small positive value that avoids dividing by zero (default 0.001). [community]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["community"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute holding community labels (default `"community"`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(u, v, score)` triples with node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `delta` is not positive, the graph is directed, or a node lacks the community attribute or does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each pair costs one neighbor-set intersection. The scores match NetworkX's `within_inter_cluster`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A and D share one within-community neighbor (B) and one outside (C): ::: {#ea3b28bf .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes( [("A", {"community": 0}), ("B", {"community": 0}), ("C", {"community": 1}), ("D", {"community": 0})] ) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D")]) round(g.within_inter_cluster([("A", "D")])[0][2], 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.999 ``` ::: :::
